summary: PostgreSQL performance degradation observed, with operations taking 4x longer than usual.
symptoms: Database backup duration increased from ~1 hour to ~4 hours.
Data synchronization between servers slowed significantly.
Queries that previously took seconds now hang for days.
High memory usage and swapping observed on one server.
mechanism: Potential Linux kernel settings and PostgreSQL configuration issues impacting I/O and memory management.

facts.evidence: PostgreSQL version mentioned in the configuration details.
Linux settings provided in the post.
Memory usage statistics provided in the post.
Performance issues described in the post.

assumptions: The database schema and workload are similar between Server A and Server B.
Linux kernel settings are contributing to the performance degradation.
unknowns: Exact query workload causing the performance degradation.
Impact of connection pooling configurations on performance.
